```{r}
#| include: false
# library(): loads a package so its functions can be used in this session.
# normalizePath(): resolves a path into a canonical absolute path.
# getwd(): returns the current working-directory path.
# file.exists(): checks whether each specified file path exists.
# file.path(): joins path components with the platform-appropriate separator.
# dirname(): returns the directory portion of a file path.
# read.csv(): reads a comma-separated file into a data frame; its first row supplies column names by default.
# read_data(): is a locally defined helper reading the specified course dataset; inspect its path and column mapping.
# factor(): stores categorical values; levels fixes their permitted order and labels can rename their display.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# theme_set(): sets the default theme for subsequent ggplot charts in this R session.
# theme_minimal(): uses a minimal chart style; base_size controls the base text size in points.
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
project <- normalizePath(getwd())
while (!file.exists(file.path(project,"20261.Rproj")) && dirname(project)!=project) project <- dirname(project)
read_data <- function(name) read.csv(file.path(project,"data/module02",name))
restaurants <- read_data("restaurant_ratings.csv")
restaurants$quality_rating <- factor(restaurants$quality_rating,levels=c("Good","Very Good","Excellent"))
audit <- read_data("audit_times.csv")
e <- read_data("electronics_sales.csv")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=14))
```

## Raw rows and summarized counts

```{r}
# ggplot(): starts a plot from data; additional layers are joined with +.
# aes(): maps variables to visual properties such as x, y, fill, color, or group.
# geom_bar(): counts records by category by default; stat="identity" instead uses supplied heights.
# labs(): sets axis titles, legend titles, plot titles, and captions.
# count(): counts rows for each combination of supplied categories.
# geom_col(): draws bars at supplied heights; it does not count records.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# all(): returns TRUE only when every supplied logical value is TRUE.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
ggplot(restaurants,aes(quality_rating))+geom_bar(fill="#2878A5")+
 labs(title="Restaurant ratings in the teaching sample",x="Quality",y="Restaurants")
counts <- restaurants |> count(quality_rating)
ggplot(counts,aes(quality_rating,n))+geom_col(fill="#2878A5")+
 labs(x="Quality",y="Restaurants")
stopifnot(all(counts$n==c(84,150,66)))
```

`geom_bar()` counts rows by default. `geom_col()` uses the supplied numerical heights.

## Numerical distribution

```{r}
# ggplot(): starts a plot from data; additional layers are joined with +.
# aes(): maps variables to visual properties such as x, y, fill, color, or group.
# geom_histogram(): bins numeric observations; binwidth or breaks controls the intervals and boundary anchors them.
# labs(): sets axis titles, legend titles, plot titles, and captions.
ggplot(audit,aes(audit_days))+
 geom_histogram(binwidth=5,boundary=10,closed="left",fill="#ACC9DA",colour="white")+
 labs(title="Distribution of audit completion times",x="Audit duration (days)",y="Audits")
```

Each bar counts audits in a five-day interval. The chosen boundaries include the lower endpoint and exclude the upper endpoint.

## Paired observations and units

```{r}
# ggplot(): starts a plot from data; additional layers are joined with +.
# aes(): maps variables to visual properties such as x, y, fill, color, or group.
# geom_point(): draws a point for each row at its mapped x and y values.
# geom_text(): draws labels from mapped data; position and hjust/vjust control placement.
# labs(): sets axis titles, legend titles, plot titles, and captions.
p <- ggplot(e,aes(commercials,sales_hundreds_usd))+
 geom_point(size=3,colour="#2878A5")+geom_text(aes(label=week),nudge_y=1)+
 labs(title="Commercials and sales across ten weeks",x="Television commercials",y="Sales (hundreds of USD)")
p
e$sales_usd <- 100*e$sales_hundreds_usd
ggplot(e,aes(commercials,sales_usd))+geom_point(size=3,colour="#2878A5")+
 labs(x="Television commercials",y="Sales (USD)")
```

Multiplying sales by 100 changes vertical units and numerical labels, while preserving the paired pattern. An unordered category needs distinct categorical encoding rather than a gradient implying magnitude or order.

## Manual export

```{r}
#| eval: false
# dir.create(): creates an output folder; recursive=TRUE creates missing parents and showWarnings=FALSE silences existing-folder warnings.
# ggsave(): saves a plot; width, height, and units define physical size and dpi defines raster resolution.
dir.create("_output",showWarnings=FALSE)
ggsave("_output/electronics-scatterplot.png",plot=p,width=8,height=4.5,dpi=150)
```

Exports belong outside input-data folders. A plot's association alone does not establish causation.
